all_of: the application is a PHP framework that renders a detailed error page instead of a generic one
some request the client can make raises an unhandled exception
any_of: a form declares a method the route does not support
the error page renders a table of environment variables or configuration values

chain.action: read the entry page and note the form's declared method and action alongside the session cookie's shape
chain.why: the declared method is what triggers the exception here, and the cookie shape tells you which session driver is in use

chain.action: submit the form exactly as declared, even if the route looks unlikely to accept that method
chain.why: an unsupported method raises a routing exception, and with debug enabled that exception is rendered as a full diagnostic page

chain.action: enumerate the labelled detail sections of the error page before reading the stack trace
chain.why: the environment section is the configuration file verbatim, which is a faster and more complete read than the trace

chain.action: take the secret from the configuration table directly
chain.why: the application key itself was the objective; no pivot or forgery was required

first_confirming_probe.request: submit the entry form using the method it declares and compare the response size with the normal page
first_confirming_probe.expected: a response an order of magnitude larger than the normal page, containing a framework exception name and labelled diagnostic sections
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the request is handled normally, or the error page is the framework's generic production page with no detail sections

blast_radius: read-only. The request raises an exception and reaches no application logic, so nothing is created or modified. Treat every credential in the disclosed configuration as live and do not connect to the services it names; they are usually bound to the container's own loopback and are out of scope.

verification.evidence: the flag was read from the body of the error page returned by the live target, inside the environment variables table as the value of the application key

reuse_when: a form's declared method does not match the route that serves the page
any response reveals a framework debug or profiler page
the application advertises a degraded or maintenance state while still answering with normal status codes
known_traps: the page's maintenance notice and the maintenance middleware in the stack trace both suggest a maintenance-mode bypass, but the application is not in maintenance mode and returns 200; that is flavour text, not the bug
the same parameter sent on the supported method is not reflected at all and the response is byte-for-byte identical to the plain page, so there is no injection surface to chase
a plain fixed-length session id means a server-side session driver, so a leaked application key does not enable a session forge on this target
